content: Lower respiratory tract infections are often equated with pneumonia, but the term also encompasses other types of infections, such as lung abscesses, acute bronchitis, and emphysema. Lower respiratory tract infections are recognized as the leading cause of death among all infectious diseases. Acute bronchitis alone affects more than 40 adults per 1,000 individuals annually. Since 1993, there has been a slight decline in the overall mortality rate associated with lower respiratory tract infections, accounting for 9% of all deaths in that year. A variety of acute and chronic infections can impact the lower respiratory tract. While antibiotics are frequently considered the first-line treatment for these infections, they are not effective or indicated in cases of viral infections. It is crucial to select antibiotics appropriately based on the specific causative organism. Furthermore, treatment regimens must adapt to the evolving nature of these infections and the increasing resistance to conventional therapies. Lower respiratory tract infections impose a significant financial burden on healthcare systems and are generally more severe than upper respiratory tract infections.
